reason: The file-level summary is highly aligned with the real `command.go` implementation and the function-level responsibilities cover almost all hollowed bodies with strong behavioral fidelity. The prompt captures inheritance rules, command discovery, flag merging, help/usage/version behavior, execution lifecycle, hook ordering, command grouping, default helper installation, and flag-set caching in enough detail to reconstruct the file with good accuracy. The few gaps are mostly small implementation details and some edge-case wording rather than major behavioral mismatches.
missing_functionality: ExecuteC also initializes the hidden `__complete` command via `initCompleteCmd(args)` before default completion command setup, which is not mentioned in the description.

ParseFlags prints buffered warning text only when parsing succeeds and new output appeared in `flagErrorBuf`; the description mentions this correctly but not that the buffer length is compared before and after parse.
updateParentsPflags reuses and accumulates a cached `parentsPflags` set rather than rebuilding it from scratch each call; this caching/reuse nuance is not explicit.

LocalFlags and InheritedFlags lazily cache synthetic flag sets and then add to them incrementally, relying on lookup checks to avoid duplicates; the prompt captures behavior but not the incremental cache-population nuance.

defaultUsageFunc and defaultHelpFunc both perform direct formatted printing and `defaultUsageFunc` ignores `fmt.Fprint/Fprintf` write errors, always returning nil; the prompt describes output content correctly but not this exact return/write-error behavior.
InitDefaultHelpCmd completion logic includes the help command itself when matching visible subcommands, by checking `subCmd == cmd.helpCommand`; this is only briefly implied.
incorrect_or_misleading_points: UsageString is described as temporarily replacing both output and error writers and invoking `Usage()` via `CheckErr`; this matches behavior, but `CheckErr` can exit on error, so describing it as simply 'capture usage output and return string' slightly understates that side effect.

ErrPrefix is described as using default prefix `Error:`; the implementation returns `"Error:"` and later printing adds a separating space externally, so readers might incorrectly reconstruct the exact formatting if they assume the space is part of the prefix.

InitDefaultVersionFlag wording says to use display name 'when the command has a name/display name'; implementation actually checks `Name() == ""` for the fallback, then uses `DisplayName()` otherwise.
execute is described as handling '`--help` as `flag.ErrHelp`'; implementation actually checks the parsed bool help flag rather than inspecting the literal token.
